fact.claim: You get $8,000 of FHSA participation room in the year you open your first FHSA. Room does not build up before the account exists: the CRA sets your carryforward to $0 in the year you open your first FHSA. After that, you can carry forward no more than $8,000 of unused room from earlier years. So each year you wait before opening one is $8,000 of deductible room you never get, though you still can't contribute more than $40,000 in total.

plain.what: An FHSA is a First Home Savings Account. It is a Canadian account that helps you save for your first home and cuts your tax when you put money in. Your room to put money in only starts the year you open your first one, so nothing is building up for you before that.
plain.so_what: Each year you wait, you skip $8,000 of room that lowers your tax, and you can never get that year back.
plain.do: Write down the year you opened your first FHSA, or write "none" if you have not opened one.
